subject: Throughput sizing & latency SLOs - FinEx

Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finex.com>

Subject: FinEx product traffic + latency targets (post-call)

Thanks again for the call today — useful discussion. Quick recap of our workload and the metrics you asked for. I attached the traffic profile CSV with per-hour QPS for the last 30 days. Highlights: 

- Primary workload: document summarization + entity extraction pipeline (single API call triggers ~1.2k tokens avg).
- Steady-state QPS: ~40 requests/sec (most weekdays 09:00-17:00 PT)
- Peak QPS observed: spikes up to ~260 QPS during batch release windows (15–30m bursts)
- Concurrent active streams during peak: ~120 connections, but only ~40 concurrent in inference at a time due to frontend pooling
- Latency SLO: p95 generation <= 350ms (hard target), p50 <= 120ms; end-to-end budget includes our pre/post processing so inference should aim ~250ms p95
- Streaming: partial token streaming is useful for UX; ideally first tokens arrive within 80–100ms and then steady streaming every 150–250ms

Questions from our side: what GPU footprint do you expect for the 260 QPS peaks for a 7B-class model (quantized)? Can you provide an initial tokens/sec and concurrency sizing? Also any recommendations to stay within the 250ms inference budget while supporting streaming?

Thanks — attaching finex_traffic_profile.csv

—Alex
Product Lead, FinEx

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Alex Thompson <alex@finex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx product traffic + latency targets (post-call)

Alex / Neha / Marissa — I pulled the attached CSV and ran a quick pass with conservative assumptions. Below is a short-form sizing we can iterate on. I include the baseline assumptions up front.

Assumptions:
- Model: 7B quantized (int8) optimized kernel, avg 1.2k tokens/request, p95 tokens/request 1.6k (using your per-request data)
- Generation tokens/sec per GPU (conservative): ~18k tokens/sec (7B int8 on A100-like instance with Redwood runtime optimizations)
- Useful batching latency headroom target (to keep p95 <= 250ms for inference): batch window <= 30ms avg, tail batching capped at 60ms
- Streaming: partial-first-token latency target <= 100ms (we can do early-first-token streaming via prefix decoding)

Sizing (back-of-envelope):
- Steady-state (40 QPS): 40 req/s * 1.2k tokens = 48k tokens/sec -> ~3 GPUs (48k / 18k ≈ 2.7)
- Peak burst (260 QPS sustained 15m): 260 * 1.6k = 416k tokens/sec -> ~24 GPUs (416k / 18k ≈ 23.1)
- If spikes are microbursts (e.g., sub-1m) we can absorb some with queueing + transient autoscale + aggressive batching; sustained 15m bursts need capacity or scheduled warmups.
- Concurrency: with streaming connections ~120 concurrent streams aligns with 24 GPU footprint above; each GPU can handle ~5–8 concurrent streams with low-latency config depending on request length and batching behavior.

Recommendations to meet p95 250ms with streaming:
- Use a low-latency model variant (7B int8 with kernel optimizations) and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Keep batch window small for tail-latency-sensitive routes (<=30ms). That reduces batching efficiency; offset with more reserved capacity for peak windows or autoscale policies that pre-warm.
- For UX: enable early-first-token streaming (we can stream logits as soon as prefix decoding completes) — first-byte within ~80–120ms is achievable at steady-state with the above config.
- Consider mixing model variants: route 10–20% of traffic to a faster distilled variant for very latency-sensitive users and the rest to the 7B quantized for higher quality. This reduces required GPUs for latency SLOs during peaks.

Cost/ops note: rough GPU counts above are conservative and ignore some optimization levers (int8 fused kernels, quantization-aware caching). We can run a short benchmark with an anonymized sample of your traffic to tighten numbers.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm p95 tokens (you mentioned 1.6k in CSV, please confirm) and spike duration pattern (sustained vs microbursts).
- Neha/Marissa: I’ll prepare two capacity options (warm reserved pool vs autoscale-heavy) and expected cost delta by Tue 3/30 EOD.

—Rafael
SRE, Serving — Redwood Inference
